subject: Help with phylogeny and data matrix difference in taxon number

messages.author: 50b36e864fb52ac0
messages.subject: Help with phylogeny and data matrix difference in taxon number
parts:
I am attempting to use the gm.prcomp function to reconstruct ancestral states in the nodes of a phylogeny consisting of 26 taxa, mapped onto a morphospace formed by 41 taxa (the 26 taxa of the phylogeny and 15 additional ones). ¿Is there a way I can do this? Whenever I try, I get an error message saying ""Error: Number of taxa in data matrix and tree are not equal.", which is understandable, but I really need a way to bypass this.
Any help would be greatly appreciated.

messages.author: fbfd20ce829c6c6c
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Help with phylogeny and data matrix difference in taxon number
parts:
One solution here would be to subset your 41 taxa down to the 26 species represented on your tree (and make sure they are in the correct order as the tip labels on your tree).
You can do this manually within R or perhaps use the treedata() function in the geiger package, there are other ways too. If using treedata(), note that it can sort the data for you with the argument sort = TRUE.

Best, 
Bryan

messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Help with phylogeny and data matrix difference in taxon number
parts:
Vicente,

 

What you desire is possible, but requires a bit of R-coding, as it is non-standard. I agree that including the 41 taxa in the GPA and then the PCA is ideal. But then you only have 26 if them with a phylogeny.

 

If you look at the underlying code for gm.prcomp you will see how the phylogeny is included in the plot (it is essentially projected into the PCA diagram).  You can use that as a template to write some modified code that uses the PCA for all 41 taxa, but then projects the phylogeny only for those species for which phylogenetic data is included.


Dean
